entries.title: Jeremiah 4:1–25
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: If - If thou wilt return, return; make no longer delay. Remove - Thou shalt not go out of thine own land into exile.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:27
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Yet - In the midst of judgment he will remember mercy.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:28
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Mourn - Expressions to set forth the dreadfulness of the judgment; he makes the elements to personate mourners.

entries.title: Jeremiah 4:31
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In travail - When the scripture would express any exquisite sorrow, it doth it by a woman in travail. First child - Which is usually the most painful. Spreadeth her hands - According to the use of persons in great anguish, clapping or wringing their hands together.
